Definition: properly, to question or hesitate, i.e. (by implication) to be reluctant
BiblicalUsage: Mahahh means to linger, to tarry, to hesitate, and it is always a delay that matters. Genesis 19:16 has Lot lingering while the angels lay hold on his hand to bring him out of Sodom, and Exodus 12:39 says Israel could not tarry when they were thrust out of Egypt. Habakkuk 2:3 says of the vision, though it tarry, wait for it, because it will surely come, and Psalms 119:60 says the psalmist made haste and delayed not to keep God's commandments.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word draws a line between two kinds of delay: Lot's lingering in Genesis 19:16 nearly cost him everything, while the tarrying in Habakkuk 2:3 is God's timing, which is never late. My position is that Psalms 119:60 is the answer to both, because haste to obey is the only delay that is safe.
